meta.title: HAZOP and LOPA of the PX-MC unit
meta.scope: From the fresh-feed battery limit (FV-101, XV-100) through the three crystallization stages (V-102 / E-101, V-202 / E-201 / C-204, V-302 / E-301 / C-304), the wash column W-104 with its melt loop (P-106, E-105), the melt drum V-401 with P-402 and the melt return, to the PX product, the reject filtrate to isomerization and the propylene jackets up to the K-501 suction header (the compressor package itself is studied by its vendor); utilities: LP steam, instrument air, power, N₂.
meta.objective: Identify the hazards and operability problems of the unit, judge their risk, and decide what must be added or changed. For the scenarios that need more than the existing safeguards, check the risk reduction by LOPA.
meta.assump: Design case: 40 t/h feed at 40 wt% PX and 20 °C; stages at 3 / −4 / −29 °C; product 99.7 wt% PX. Trained operators. Design pressures, PSVs, N₂ blankets and the MDMT are assumed where the OTS marks them so. Instruments and trips are proof tested yearly (LOPA tab, T = 1 yr). Risk matrix and target event frequencies are those of the OTS HAZID and LOPA tabs (teaching values).
meta.protocol: Method: HAZOP to IEC 61882 with full recording. The team takes one node at a time, states its design intent, and applies the guide words to each parameter to find deviations. For each deviation it records the causes, the events that follow, the consequences without credit for safeguards, the existing safeguards, and the risk after safeguards (S × L). Rows above the tolerable level go to LOPA in the same worksheet: initiating-event frequency, enabling conditions and conditional modifiers, independent protection layers with their PFD, and the mitigated frequency compared with the tolerable event likelihood for the severity. Open points go to the Parking Lot; actions become recommendations with an owner and a due date.

TV-403 fails open on instrument-air failure (TI-403 137 °C at 30 min, model)
TIC-403 transmitter low
N6.cons: Xylene above its flash point and close to boiling: vapour from the vent or PSV, fire; overpressure of V-401
N6.notes:
Worked example
LOPA (worked example): values from the OTS LOPA tab, scenario L2. No IPL is credited in the present design: TIC-403 is the loop that failed (no air), there is no high-temperature alarm, and PSV-401 protects V-401 against rupture, not against vapour leaving the vent. TEL for S4 = 1e-3 per year (the OTS LOPA tab). After R01 the new SIF-07 (TSHH-403 → steam XV, PFD 0.01725, SIL 1) gives f_mit = 2.59e-04 per year, which meets the TEL.

recs.text: Add TAH-403 and an independent TSHH-403 that closes a steam shut-off valve on the V-401 coil; change TV-403 to fail closed. On the model an air failure takes TI-403 to 137 °C in 30 min (xylene boils at ≈ 138 °C).
Thermal relief, or car-sealed-open valves under MOC, wherever a steam-heated side can be blocked in with liquid (E-105 process side, V-401 coil).
Low-level protection for P-402 on V-401 (LSLL stopping P-402) and a check of the existing low-flow behaviour.
LSHH-405 must also stop C-204 and C-304 (the cake feeding V-401). Closing the feed alone lets V-401 reach 128 % on the model; stopping the centrifuges holds it at 93 %. (Raised by the SRS review.)
Start-up sequence: open the melt return (FIC-402) before the feed and confirm DIC-115 in cascade; add a permissive on FI-402.
Detect propylene in the slurry (jacket leak): V-401 vent hydrocarbon monitor or periodic analysis; route the V-401 vent to a safe place.
